changesets.summary: Let the host decide the agent loop's language, tools, context and spend. `createAgent({ messages })` replaces every sentence the loop writes into a request or a result (`AgentMessages`; the English `AGENT_MESSAGES` are byte for byte the earlier text), and passes `messages.goal`, `messages.recall`, `messages.environment` and `messages.toolbox` to the goal prompt, the `recall` and environment tools and its own toolboxes; `createLedger({ messages: { goal } })`, `goalPrompt(goal, messages)`, `createRecallTool(ledger, { messages })`, `environmentTools(environment, messages)` and `createToolbox({ messages })` take the same words. `recall` is now listed only when the agent can compact (a ledger and a `historyBudget`), or with `recall: true`; `recall: false` never lists it. Tools run as `execute(input, { signal, context })` with the send's abort signal and the host's `toolContext`, so a stopped run stops its tools (Jaren's contract tools read the same signal). A model call that rejects counts as a turn and carries `error.partial = { messages, steps, spent }`. `budget.cost` bounds a run priced by `prices(model)`, `spend()` reports `cost`, and `budget.reserve` with `maxOutputTokens` refuses any call whose worst case could cross the token or cost budget, booking the worst case when a provider reports no usage; `probePrices` in `@tangleai/models/providers` reads per-token prices from a provider's model listing. `toolbox.add` throws `AI0001` for a name it already holds unless `{ replace: true }`, and `toolboxFromContract(contract, client, { bind, mapOutcome, … })` registers a contract's operations with host-bound input members removed from the model's schema and injected on execution.

Report scanned PDFs and let a host read them. A PDF whose pages carry no text answers its empty elements with an `image-only` warning. An `ocr: { version, read }` hook on `extractPdf`, `extractDocument` and `createDocumentIngester` reads each page without text through the host's own OCR (`read({ page, width, height, pdf })` answers the page's text or `{ text, bbox? }` lines), whose text becomes elements in page order beside an `ocr` warning; the hook's `version` enters the ingester's extraction identity, so a document read with and without OCR never shares a version.

Keep the API key out of every client object. `client.endpoint` is the credential-free identity `{ provider, base, url, model, hasKey }`; the headers, key included, stay inside the client, so logging, serializing or inspecting a chat client, or a routed client over it, never shows them, and a provider error body that echoes the key has it replaced by `[redacted]` in the `AI0002` message. Migration: read `hasKey` instead of `endpoint.headers`; `resolveEndpoint` still returns the headers to the caller that passed the key. A base URL with a username or password, or with a scheme other than `http:` or `https:`, is refused with `AI0001` when the client is built, and no refusal quotes credentials or a query. The routed client codes its own failures: a deadline is `AI0004` (`outcome: 'timeout'`, `deadlineMs`), a reply over its token ceiling `AI0005` (`outcome: 'token-limit'`, `usage`, `limit`) and an account stop `AI0006` (`outcome: 'budget'`); a caller's own abort still rejects with the caller's reason.

Report structured-output failures in one shape and stop repairing truncated replies. `createStructuredOutput().generate` answers `{ ok: true, value }` or `{ ok: false, errors }`, both with `raw`, `attempts`, `finishReason`, summed `usage` and per-attempt `calls`; every error record carries `stage` (`parse`, `schema`, `gate` or `truncated`), an always-present `code` and `path`, and `message`, beside the `instancePath`, `keyword` and `docPath` the repair prompt still carries byte for byte. A reply that stops at the token limit, or carries reasoning and no content, is reported as `truncated` instead of being sent for a repair; `onAttempt` reports a reply that is not JSON as `parse` (it said `schema`) and adds each attempt's finish reason and usage. A passing gate may return `data`, surfaced as `gateData`; `deadlineMs` bounds a whole generation as `AI0004`; `parse: 'lenient'` reads JSON wrapped in prose; `bundle: true` sends `bundleSchema(schema, refs)`, a self-contained schema, while validation stays local; `tier` overrides the structured-output tier. The chat client states its model's tier (`structured`, reported as `endpoint.structured`, so Anthropic models on OpenRouter can take the prompt-carried `null` they need, since they refuse `oneOf`), bounds each attempt with `timeoutMs` (a retryable `AI0002` with status 0), and asks a stream for its usage with `requestUsage` (`stream_options`, never in the replay key). `createRoutedClient` accepts a host's own purpose and types its `onRoute` events and `account`. New entries: `@tangleai/models/testing` exports `createScriptedFetch`, a scripted `fetch` for keyless tests (replies, truncation, HTTP and network failures, a hang that honours abort), and `@tangleai/models/replay-file` exports `createFileReplayCache`, a replay directory over an injected file system with `record`, `fresh` and a fail-closed `replay` mode. `ChatResult`, `ChatClient`, `StructuredError` and `StructuredResult` are exported types. The program runtime's `account` option takes typed `reserve` and `settle` functions.

Tooling: the Jaren bootstrap runs npm through the npm CLI that launched it, without a shell, so `npm run jaren:bootstrap` runs on Windows as on Linux. `compose/searxng.yml` serves SearxNG for the grounding web diagnostic; the web run keeps its model calls in the wire cache and its name resolutions beside its HTTP capture, `--web-replay` rebuilds a recorded run with zero network calls and fails unless its report identity is reproduced, and `--web-structured` sets the model's structured-output tier. The diagnostic ran on 2026-11-04 with Anthropic's Haiku 5.5 and replays byte for byte. The graph-retrieval live registration moves to Haiku 5.5 with every schema carried in the prompt. Every workspace now depends on the others at the exact suite version, so an install never mixes two Tangle releases. The interactive `changeset` command is gone with `@changesets/cli` and its 14 development packages: release intent is a hand-written `.changeset/<name>.md` file (see `.changeset/README.md`), and changelogs are written by `@changesets/changelog-git`, as before. Development audit findings in `launch-editor` and `shell-quote` are gone with it.
